modules.comment: IMPORT-ORDER RULE: the CANONICAL module for a shared input sheet must be listed FIRST. The first-imported module claims the workbook-scoped X_Cell_*/X_Table_* named ranges and keeps its input sheet unrenamed as the master. Enteric and Manure both ship an 'Input - Pasture Beef' sheet that backs the same 17 named ranges, but 7 of them sit at different rows (Enteric's date/digestibility block is ~7 rows higher than Manure's). Manure is the master, so it is imported before Enteric_BeefPasture.

Enteric's 'Input - Pasture Beef' sheet is now identical (same rows) to the canonical copy imported by ManureManagement_BeefPasture, so it is intentionally excluded here via 'include' (only the calculation sheet is imported). Enteric's calculation formulas resolve inputs by workbook-scoped named range, so they still bind correctly to Manure's copy of the sheet.
Pasture beef has its own fertiliser production systems inputs.

Pasture beef only needs the pasture residue chain. The workbook now ships crop- and pasture-specific leaching/runoff sheets, so this imports Input - Pasture plus 6.2 Pasture residue N2O and 6.3 Leach runoff pasture (which depends only on the pasture residue sheet and Input - Pasture, not on any crop sheet or Input - Crop). The crop input, 6.1 Crop residue N2O and 6.4 Residue burning are not required. A bare string (like the entries above) imports every sheet the registry lists for that module; this object form subsets them.
Scope 3 contains livestock purchase inputs that are not required here as there is already a livestock purchases module in Pasture Beef herd movement

menu.comment: The column-A navigation menu is regenerated on every sheet from the final sheet set. Groups are assigned automatically: Home/Results = untitled; any sheet named 'Input*' = INPUTS; calculation sheets = CALCULATIONS; everything else = APPENDICES. 'labels' overrides the link text for a sheet (default derivation strips the 'Input - ' prefix, otherwise uses the sheet name). Set enabled=false to leave existing menus untouched.
